stem: Researchers _____ new methods to improve the accuracy of the study.
explanation: "Researchers" is plural, so the auxiliary is "have"; the present perfect connects recent work to the present.

stem: If she had studied harder, she _____ the exam.
explanation: The third conditional (if + past perfect, would have + past participle) describes an imaginary past result.

stem: If I had taken that job, I _____ in London now.
explanation: A mixed conditional links an imaginary past action to a present result; "now" rules out would have lived.

stem: _____ you need any help, please contact the department office.
explanation: "Should you need" is a formal inverted form of "If you need".

stem: I wish I _____ more attention in class last year.
explanation: "Wish" + past perfect expresses regret about the past.

stem: Provided that the weather _____ good, the ceremony will be held outdoors.
explanation: After "provided that" (= if), use the present simple to refer to the future.

stem: The data _____ by two independent researchers before publication.
explanation: The passive (were checked) is needed because the data did not perform the action; in academic English "data" is often treated as plural.

stem: The new policy is expected _____ next month.
explanation: The passive infinitive (to be implemented) is used because the policy receives the action.

stem: The building must _____ before the new semester begins.
explanation: A modal passive is modal + be + past participle: must be repaired.

stem: It _____ that the ancient city was destroyed by an earthquake.
explanation: The impersonal passive "It is believed that..." is common in academic writing.

stem: I had my laptop _____ at the campus repair shop.
explanation: The causative "have something done" uses the past participle: had my laptop fixed.

stem: The professor _____ I spoke is an expert in marine biology.
explanation: In formal English, a preposition can come before "whom" in a relative clause: to whom I spoke.

stem: The period _____ the experiment took place was unusually dry.
explanation: "During which" introduces a relative clause about a period of time in formal writing.

stem: The article, _____ was published last month, caused a lot of debate.
explanation: A non-defining relative clause (between commas) uses "which", not "that".

stem: She passed all her exams, _____ surprised everyone.
explanation: "Which" can refer to a whole previous clause in a non-defining relative clause.

stem: _____ the report, the manager called an urgent meeting.
explanation: A perfect participle clause (Having read) shows that one action was completed before the next.

stem: Students _____ in the program must attend an orientation session.
explanation: A reduced relative clause uses a participle: students (who are) enrolled in the program.

stem: _____ in 1850, the university is one of the oldest in the region.
explanation: A past participle clause (Founded) has a passive meaning: the university was founded.

stem: Last month, the manager said that the report _____ by the following Friday.
explanation: Reported from a past point of view ("the following Friday"), "will" changes to "would".

stem: She asked me _____ I had ever been to Japan.
explanation: Reported yes/no questions are introduced by "if" or "whether".

stem: The professor suggested that each student _____ a topic by Monday.
explanation: After "suggest that" in formal English, the subjunctive (base form) is used: that each student choose.

stem: I regret _____ you that your application was unsuccessful.
explanation: "Regret to inform" is used to announce bad news; "regret doing" means being sorry about a past action.

stem: I regret _____ so much time on social media last year.
explanation: "Regret + -ing" expresses being sorry about something you did in the past.

stem: If the printer doesn't work, try _____ it off and on again.
explanation: "Try + -ing" means to do something as an experiment to see if it solves a problem.

stem: He objected to _____ like a child.
explanation: "Object to" is followed by an -ing form; the passive gerund is being + past participle.

stem: She is used to _____ in a noisy environment.
explanation: "Be used to" (be accustomed to) is followed by a noun or -ing form.

stem: The committee is responsible _____ reviewing all applications.
explanation: The adjective "responsible" is followed by "for".

stem: The success of the project depends _____ careful planning.
explanation: The verb "depend" is followed by "on".

stem: Air pollution has contributed _____ an increase in asthma cases.
explanation: The verb "contribute" is followed by "to".

stem: There has been a sharp increase _____ the price of housing.
explanation: "An increase in" is used for the thing that rises; "an increase of" is used for the amount.

stem: The study focuses on how children learn, what motivates them, and _____.
explanation: Items in a list should have the same grammatical form (parallel structure): how..., what..., and how...

stem: The course teaches students to think critically, to write clearly, and _____ effectively.
explanation: Parallel structure requires the same form in each item: to think, to write, and to communicate.

stem: Not only _____ the exam, but she also received the highest score.
explanation: When a sentence begins with "Not only", the subject and auxiliary are inverted: did she pass.

stem: The results were _____ surprising that the team repeated the experiment.
explanation: "So" + adjective + "that" introduces a result.

stem: I'd rather you _____ your phone during the lecture.
explanation: "Would rather" + another subject is followed by the past simple for present or future meaning.

stem: She left early _____ she could catch the last train.
explanation: "So that" + clause expresses purpose; "in order to" is followed by a base verb, not a clause.

stem: _____ the high cost, many students choose to live off campus.
explanation: "Due to" is followed by a noun phrase; because, since and as need a full clause.

stem: _____ he is intelligent, he often struggles with exams.
explanation: "While" can introduce a contrasting clause; despite and in spite of need a noun or -ing form.

stem: Scarcely had the meeting begun _____ the fire alarm went off.
explanation: The fixed pattern is "scarcely/hardly ... when" ("no sooner ... than").

stem: The findings _____ that the treatment may be effective.
explanation: "Findings" is plural, so the verb is "suggest". Reporting verbs like suggest are used for cautious academic claims.

stem: These results _____ be interpreted with caution because the sample was small.
explanation: "Should be interpreted" expresses a recommendation; "must to" and "ought" (without "to") are incorrect.

stem: The _____ of new technology has transformed the way students learn.
explanation: After "The" and before "of", a noun is needed: the introduction of.

stem: Each of the participants _____ asked to complete a questionnaire.
explanation: "Each" is singular, so the verb is singular: was asked.

stem: A number of students _____ complained about the new schedule.
explanation: "A number of" means "several" and takes a plural verb: have complained.

stem: The team of scientists _____ working on a new vaccine.
explanation: The head noun is "team" (singular), so the verb is singular: is working. ("of scientists" does not change the agreement.)

stem: By 2030, the city _____ its public transport network.
explanation: The future perfect (will have + past participle) describes an action completed before a future time.

stem: The seminar _____ for an hour when the power went out.
explanation: The past perfect continuous shows the duration of an activity up to a moment in the past.

stem: _____ knowledge is not the same as wisdom.
explanation: Abstract uncountable nouns used in a general sense take no article: Knowledge is...

stem: She has made _____ progress this term.
explanation: "Progress" is uncountable, so it takes "a great deal of", not many/several.

stem: It was not until the 1950s _____ the disease was fully understood.
explanation: The cleft structure is "It was not until ... that ...".

stem: The results were _____ different from what we expected.
explanation: An adjective (different) is modified by an adverb: significantly.

stem: Her _____ to the project was praised by everyone.
explanation: After "Her" and before "to the project" we need the noun for the action: contribution.
